_about: WHAT THE RUN ASKS OF THE ENGINE'S OPTIONAL PERFORMANCE FEATURES, and of the port's own per-frame diagnostics.
Planning step 190 of docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (ENG-3). Read by sim/EngineTuning; main.cpp turns it into the
engine's GameManifest fields (engine/src/core/GameRuntime.hpp) and the layer's Paths::spriteReport. A table that will not read leaves the
engine AS IT WAS, with a WARN in the log. The log's third line says what the run was given: 'engine options (a player's run): ...'.
A player's run (attended_run) is a window the game opened for someone to play (game/RunKind.hpp, AttendedRun); every capture, route, level
walk and script is 'other_runs'. The flags --shadow-maps, --sprites-only, --asset-watching, --sprite-report and --perf-log override this
table for ONE run (an A/B: one exe, one setting changed). To decline a value, change it here: no code changes, no relink.
Each value is a MEASURED decision. The rule it had to meet: every picture byte for byte what it was (the 19 classic baselines in 9 variants, 162 launches,
the 128-level f420 sweep under three configurations, the S/R/W pictures) AND a measured gain on a named metric. All measurements: Magic Portals Enhanced, AMD
Radeon 780M (integrated), Windows 11, 1280x720, present mode FIFO (60 fps), Vulkan validation layers ON, MagicPortals.exe a0a9f233, 2026-10-16;
medians of 3 interleaved launches (the numbers are for A/B, not a player's frame rate).
shadow_map_resolution 16 (KEPT): no sprite samples a shadow map. The developer's lit boxes do: with the B key pressed over level12b's art,
165,280 of 921,600 pixels (17.9%) differ between 16 px and the engine's own sizes (the boxes' shadows are gone; a real-time run, a synthetic
B keypress); a level run with an empty --art folder gives 166,165 (18.0%) and level0 8; --shadow-maps 0 brings them back. The art view,
which is what a player sees, is byte for byte the same. The GPU memory of the process (Windows' per-process counter, level12b at
5 s) fell from 350.6 to 157.8 MiB dedicated (-192.8; total committed 410.9 to 218.2), on both launches of each; pictures identical.
The engine's own sizes are 4 x 2048 + 2 x 1024 + 2 x 1024 D32 (120 MiB by arithmetic; the counter also holds the driver's alignment).
sprites_only_scene_pipelines false (DECLINED; the mechanism stays, --sprites-only on): every draw this port puts through the scene pipelines is
unlit (a sprite, a particle, a halo), so the four pipelines can be built with the lit surface folded away, and with it on every picture was byte
for byte what it was (the 19 baselines, the 128-level sweep, the S/R/W pictures). Declined because no gain could be measured here and a small
cost was: the four scene pipelines take 37 ms (35..48) to create at every warm start against 31 ms (29..36) plain, 13 launches each (retaken on
the final exe, 6 launches each: 37.5 ms (36..44) against 35.5 (33..40), so the cost is 2 to 6 ms at every warm start); the first
compile ever is cheaper (315 ms against 641 ms, two single cold launches on different days, not a controlled pair); and no GPU time can be
measured on a 60 fps FIFO machine. The gain the engine's author measured is on an Adreno 640 (a 2D menu in 75 ms instead of 117): when a phone
build exists, set this true and take the pictures gate there. The cost of true: the developer's lit boxes (the B key, and a level drawn without
its art) draw flat; --sprites-only off brings them back.
asset_watching attended_run false (KEPT): the engine stats every watched file on every frame for a developer's hot reload and hashes every
material's paths. Process CPU time over a 600-frame run (GetProcessTimes), on versus off: still level 2562 (2219..2891) to 2016 (1922..2062)
ms, route 2703 to 2359 ms, scrolling 1875 to 1594 ms (420 frames): 0.57 to 0.91 ms of CPU per frame, the ranges not overlapping (retaken on
the final exe: still 0.57, scrolling 0.78, route 0.68). Pictures identical. The wall time of 600 frames is the same on and off (about 10.9 s:
a FIFO loop is paced by the display). other_runs stays true so parity work keeps hot reload.
sprite_report attended_run true (DECLINED): the layer's per-frame walk over its sprites for the 'on'/'off'/'GONE' log lines. Game Layers
median 0.1514 ms on, 0.1479 off (ranges overlap, the noise floor is about 0.004 ms), no change on the scrolling or route runs; in a real
console window the first second's worst frame is 214 to 219 ms either way. Not kept: nothing measurable. The switch stays (--sprite-report).
mobile (planning step 201, PORT-3; made to take effect by step 205, PORT-7): the PHONE PROFILE, laid over the answers above for a run under it. A phone's
build runs under it by default (game/BuildProfile.hpp kMobileBuild); `--profile mobile` asks the same of a desktop run, `--profile desktop` the other
way. A desktop run never applies the block, but this file is checked whole when it is loaded, so a typo in it fails where the file is read. Its keys are
described in the block itself. Nothing in it has been measured on a phone: no phone has run this port.
Step 205 turned two of the declined candidates above ON for the phone profile only, on the strength of the same byte-for-byte picture rule: the block's
sprites_only_scene_pipelines true and sprite_report false. The top-level values above stay what they are (the desktop's). The sample cap has a key and is
ABSENT: it is still the owner's decision (see the block's _owner_decisions). Dynamic resolution has its keys and, since step 244, is ON for the phone profile
(the block's _decided says on whose word and why: a trade of the HUD's sharpness against a GPU's speed, measured on no phone).
THE PHONE PROFILE: each key here, when present, REPLACES the answer above for a run under the profile (sim/EngineTuning.hpp MobileBlock). A key
left out leaves the desktop's answer. The keys, and only these (any other key that does not begin with an underscore is refused by name):
minimum_vulkan_minor 1 (or 2): the lowest Vulkan 1.x a GPU must report to be used; GameManifest::minimumVulkanMinor (engine/src/core/GameRuntime.hpp:89,
clamped into 1 to 2 by GameRuntime.cpp:117). Without it the engine wants 1.2, and the stock drivers of many phones on Android 11 and 12 report 1.1: no GPU is
acceptable, the device constructor throws and the start ends before its first frame. Source: the sibling port Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows Enhanced, its
step E39, where two testers' phones (an Oppo A54 on Android 11, Vulkan 1.1.131, and an A74 5G on Android 12, 1.1.128) opened to a black screen and the home
screen, and the engine's author states that it uses nothing newer than 1.1 core (GameRuntime.hpp). Decoded from that record and the engine's code; NOT measured
here, on any phone. Unverified on a 1.1 driver: the scene fragment stage uses 8 of one known GPU's 8 combined fragment resources (Penumbra E39).
This is a START/NO-START matter and not a tuning one, which is why it is a key at all and the desktop leaves it out: a desktop run asks for 1.2, the engine's own.
shadow_map_resolution 16: as the top-level key, repeated on purpose. The top-level 16 is a desktop decision (step 190: no sprite samples a shadow map, 192.8 MiB
of GPU memory saved on a 780M); on a phone the system's low-memory manager counts those bytes, and the sibling port's E43 took the same 16 for it. Written here
so that a developer who sets the top-level key to 0 to see the lit boxes' shadows does not move a phone with it.
asset_watching false: the engine's per-frame stat of every watched file (step 190: 0.57 to 0.91 ms of CPU a frame on the desktop). On a phone the texture keys are
virtual and not files at all, so every stat fails every frame (engine/src/core/GameRuntime.hpp, assetWatching). A plain true/false, for both kinds of run: a
phone has nobody to hot-reload a saved file for. A desktop run's attended answer is already false, so for a player the key says it again.
sprites_only_scene_pipelines true (planning step 205): the four scene pipelines are built with the lit surface folded away (GameManifest::spritesOnlyScenePipelines).
A plain true/false, for both kinds of run. PROVENANCE. The picture rule is this port's and was MEASURED on a desktop: with it on, every picture was byte for byte what it
was (step 190: the 19 baselines, the 128-level sweep, the S/R/W pictures; step 205 retook it under `--profile mobile`: the 19 baselines and the unedited 128-level
f420 sweep, plain and classic, byte-equal to the desktop's). The GAIN is NOT measured on this port and is the sibling's, on an Adreno 640: a 2D menu drew in 75 ms
instead of 117 and a level in 25 instead of 33 (Penumbra E41). On the owner's desktop it cost 2 to 6 ms at every warm start (step 190) and gained nothing a 60 fps FIFO
machine can show; that is why the top-level key stays false. THE COST of true: the developer's lit boxes (the B key, and a level drawn without its art) draw FLAT under
it; `--sprites-only off` (a developer's flag) or the top-level desktop answer brings them back. A player never sees them.
sprite_report false (planning step 205): the layer's per-frame walk over its sprites that writes an 'on'/'off'/'GONE' line when one crosses the view. A plain
true/false, for both kinds of run. Nothing measurable on a desktop (step 190: Game Layers 0.1514 ms on, 0.1479 off, the ranges overlapping); a phone writes every log
line to flash. It changes no pixel and no tick. The G key's dump of every sprite is kept whatever this says.
scene_samples (planning step 205; ABSENT, which is the owner's decision NOT yet taken): 1, 2 or 4, the scene target's sample cap (GameManifest::sceneSamples). Absent
is the desktop's answer, the engine's own (the device's best, at most 4). The cost of a phone's 4: 44 B per pixel more than 1 (92 MiB at 2.2 megapixels, step 205's
arithmetic and the platform research's section 3b); what a smaller cap does to this port's PIXELS is measured in step 205 with `--scene-samples` and is the owner's to
judge, together with edge_cover.enabled (game/data/edge_cover.json: its strips were built around 4 samples). `--scene-samples <1|2|4>` tries a value for one run.
dynamic_resolution (planning step 205 built it; step 244 turned it ON, enabled TRUE): the scene target sized by how fast the GPU draws it
(engine/src/core/DynamicResolution.hpp). All seven keys are required when the object is present. The NUMBERS ARE THE SIBLING'S, Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows
Enhanced's E41 and E47 (its game/main.cpp), and have NOT been measured on this port or on any phone: min_scale 0.3, target_fps 58.0 (E41); relaxed_rise true,
min_target_height 360, emergency_below_fps 30.0 (E47, found on a Galaxy A05). start_max_pixels is 0 and NOT the sibling's 2200000: 0 is NO start budget (the engine lowers
the start scale only when the budget is above 0 and under the window's pixel count, SupersonicApp.cpp), and a budget under a phone's window (1,152,000 pixels at 1600x720)
would downscale EVERY phone for good on a driver that offers only a display-paced present, where the controller can only fall. So a run starts at the full size and the
controller steps down on a phone that needs it, at the price of a few seconds of slow frames on the weakest. The controller needs an unpaced loop to rise, and the HUD and
the touch controls are drawn into the smaller picture and blur with it (the platform research's PL-09). TO TURN IT OFF: set enabled false here. A run can turn it off or on
without editing the file with `--dynamic-res off` or `on` (these numbers). The engine never applies it to a capture, a --fixed-step run, a replay or a recording, so no
captured pixel can move.

dynamic_resolution._provenance: EVERY number here is a guess: measured on no phone. min_scale 0.3 and target_fps 58.0 are the sibling's E41 (Penumbra, Castle of Shadows Enhanced); relaxed_rise true, min_target_height 360 and emergency_below_fps 30.0 are its E47 (a Galaxy A05). start_max_pixels 0 is this port's own (step 244), not the sibling's 2200000: see the block's _about. What they come to on a phone held in landscape (a window 720 lines high): the floor of 360 lines is a scale of 0.5 (800x360 at 1600x720), reached from 1.0 in one step at most (a step at most halves the scale), and the emergency floor of 0.3 (480x216) only on a window that ran under 30 fps AT that floor. Cost follows the pixel count in the sibling's measurement (an Adreno 640: half the width and height, about 4x the speed), which is not this port on a PowerVR.

_decided.sprites_only_scene_pipelines: IN for the phone profile (step 205): byte-identical in every picture of this port on a desktop (steps 190 and 205), the measured gain is the sibling's. Costs the developer's lit boxes, which draw flat.
_decided.sprite_report: IN for the phone profile (step 205): false. Changes no pixel and no tick.
_decided.dynamic_resolution: ON for the phone profile (step 244), under the owner's general word of 2026-11-15, verbatim: "you are allowed to fix everytihn , commit and push under my name only and make a new release." That is a delegation and not a ruling of his on this lever: it was taken as the word to turn on the sibling's mitigation for one player's report, a Galaxy A03 Core (SM-A032M/DS, PowerVR GE8322, 2 GB, Android 11 Go) whose first level runs 'frame by frame'. THE CAUSE OF THAT REPORT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: nothing was measured on any phone, and the lever helps only if the lag is pixel-bound (the level draws every blended sprite into a window-sized RGBA16F 4x-MSAA target, which a menu does not; that is an inference). The price: the HUD and the touch controls blur with the scaled target (the sibling's A05 tester complained of pixelation), each step down recreates the target (a hitch), and the controller needs a few seconds of slow frames to judge. One key undoes it: enabled false.

_owner_decisions.scene_samples: STILL THE OWNER'S, with edge_cover.enabled (the platform research's PL-05, owner decision 1; dynamic resolution left this bundle at step 244, see _decided): 1 or 2 samples would save 44 or 24 B per pixel of the scene target but move some edge pixels in a project whose gate is pixels. Step 205 built the key (absent here) and the flag and MEASURED the pixel cost; it decided nothing, and step 244 did not touch it.
_owner_decisions.dynamic_resolution.enabled: TAKEN at step 244 under the owner's general word of 2026-11-15 (see _decided), not ruled on by him: whether the HUD and the controls may blur with the scene target (the platform research's PL-09, owner decision 3) is the part of it he was not asked, and to reverse the whole decision is the one key enabled false. The numbers are the sibling's, written with their provenance and marked as guesses.
_owner_decisions.edge_cover.enabled: STILL THE OWNER'S: game/data/edge_cover.json is not touched by the phone profile.
